$comment: Value-domain inventory read by scripts/lint-schema-value-domains.cjs. Each concept states its meaning, its value domain, and exactly one kernel type: the one schema that every use of the concept references, or "to be named" until a later change names it. A match rule is the test that finds a schema declaring the concept inline instead of referencing its kernel type. A properties rule matches a schema that declares every listed name, whatever else it declares; exact limits it to the listed names. A concept with a match rule lists its sources: every inline copy in the tree today. The lint fails on a copy that sources doesn't list, and on a listed copy that is gone. Regenerate sources with node scripts/lint-schema-value-domains.cjs --update-sources, and review the diff: a source should only disappear because its site now references the kernel type. homonyms lists property names that carry more than one meaning, with the reason. distinct_structures lists named schemas that share one structure but are distinct concepts, with the reason a receiver treats them differently.

value_domains.identity: What names a record, compared by exact equality and never parsed or shown as prose.
value_domains.reference: An object that points at a record another party holds, such as an account, a brand, a format, or a list.
value_domains.money: An amount of money and the currency it is counted in.
value_domains.time: A point in time, a calendar date, a span between two of them, a duration, or a time zone.
value_domains.code: A value from a list that a standard or this protocol fixes, such as a currency code, a language tag, or a task status.
value_domains.envelope: A structure the protocol wraps around every task request and response, such as the task envelope, context, extensions, and errors.

concepts.meaning: An amount of money in one currency, such as a budget, a fee, a credit limit, or a spend cap. The amount and its ISO 4217 currency code travel together in one object.
concepts.$comment: A schema that declares amount and currency next to other fields, such as a price with a billing period or a pricing option, counts: its amount and currency are one money value declared inline.

concepts.meaning: An ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code, three uppercase letters, such as USD or EUR.
The response that tells a caller its task was accepted to run asynchronously, and carries the task_id the caller polls or receives a webhook for.
concepts.$comment: A copy that adds fields, such as replayed or expected_confirmation_at, counts. Three acknowledgements without errors don't: the two get_creative_features copies forbid errors and carry evaluation_id, and preview_creative's submitted branch adds the response_type discriminator. Each defines its own acknowledgement, so the rule lists errors.

concepts.meaning: The progress payload of a task that is still running.
concepts.$comment: The rule leaves out context and ext. The progress objects of the task status responses carry the same four fields without them, and they are the progress of a running task.

concepts.meaning: The payload of a task that paused for buyer input or approval.
concepts.$comment: This rule matches the exact set of names. The root of media-buy/request-proposals-response.json declares all five names among many others, and it is a final response, not a paused task.

concepts.meaning: The lifecycle state of a task, such as submitted, working, input-required, completed, or failed.
Caller data that a request carries and the response echoes back unchanged, so the caller can correlate the two.
Implementation-specific fields that sit outside the protocol, which a receiver may ignore.
One error a task reports: its code, its message, and where it applies.
The protocol version fields every request and response carries.
The fields every task response carries around its task-specific payload.
How a caller asks for one page of a list.
How a response describes the page it returns and how to fetch the next one.

A calendar day, written as an RFC 3339 full-date, with no time of day or time zone.

A reference to a creative format, by the agent that defines it and the format ID there.
A reference to a signal, by the agent that publishes it and the signal ID there.

A reference to a collection list that a governance agent hosts.
The ID of a record, minted by the party that holds the record and carried back unchanged by every other party. Receivers compare it by exact equality and never parse it.
concepts.$comment: The four ID concepts share one rule: any inline x-entity string that no reference concept names. Each copy is listed under one of them. The ID classes, and the rule that assigns each entity to one class, come in a later PR.

concepts.meaning: The ID of a record, restricted to letters, digits, and _ . : -, so it is safe in URLs, file names, and logs. It may be bounded in length.
concepts.$comment: The four ID concepts share one rule: any inline x-entity string that no reference concept names. Each copy is listed under one of them. The ID classes, and the rule that assigns each entity to one class, come in a later PR.

concepts.meaning: The ID of a record, written as a lowercase slug of letters, digits, and underscores.

homonyms.name: as_of
homonyms.reason: A calendar date where a geo region support snapshot is a whole day, and a timestamp everywhere else.

homonyms.name: brand_id
homonyms.reason: An advertiser brand ID names a brand in an advertiser's parent organization's portfolio; a rights-holder brand ID names a brand in a rights agent's roster. The entity registry keeps them apart even where the strings look alike.

homonyms.name: end
homonyms.reason: A date range ends on a calendar date; every other range ends at an instant.

homonyms.name: evidence_id
homonyms.reason: Audience evidence backs an audience claim; governance adjustment evidence backs a governance adjustment. Each names a record of its own entity.

homonyms.name: last_updated
homonyms.reason: A calendar date where the version-1 canonical mapping registry's update is a whole day, and a timestamp everywhere else.

homonyms.name: list_id
homonyms.reason: A property list and a collection list are separate records on a governance agent. list_id names one or the other, by the reference that holds it.

homonyms.name: occurred_at
homonyms.reason: A calendar date where an out-of-home posting is a whole day, and a timestamp everywhere else.

homonyms.name: offering_id
homonyms.reason: A sponsored-intelligence offering and a reporting delivery offering are different records; the reporting one is a bounded token.

homonyms.name: policy_id
homonyms.reason: A policy entry can describe a registry policy or an inline policy. Task payloads embed only inline entries, so a policy entry's policy_id names an inline policy. Everywhere else, policy_id names a policy the shared registry publishes.

homonyms.name: pricing_option_id
homonyms.reason: A product pricing option belongs to a seller's product; a vendor pricing option belongs to a vendor's offer, such as a signal or a creative service.

homonyms.name: start
homonyms.reason: A date range starts on a calendar date; every other range starts at an instant.

homonyms.name: valid_from
homonyms.reason: A calendar date where a business calendar's validity or a seasonal availability or rate window starts on a whole day, and a timestamp everywhere else.

homonyms.name: valid_to
homonyms.reason: A calendar date where a seasonal availability or rate window ends on a whole day, and a timestamp everywhere else.

homonyms.name: valid_until
homonyms.reason: A calendar date where a measurement accreditation's expiry is a whole day, and a timestamp everywhere else.

distinct_structures.reason: Each points at a list on a governance agent by agent_url and list_id. A receiver resolves a property list reference against property lists and a collection list reference against collection lists; list_id names a different entity in each (x-entity property_list and collection_list).

Each is a bounded opaque string, and a receiver processes them differently: a file object reference is a destination-relative object key that providers URI-encode; a native version reference is a provider version token that is never URI-encoded or joined to an object reference.
Each is the body of a separate task: one acts on collection lists, the other on property lists. Their list_id names a different entity, and a receiver routes each to its own task.
